newsitem.title: USA: Compromise reached in Texas church dispute.
newsitem.headline: Compromise reached in Texas church dispute.

text.p: Church officials have agreed not to raze the historic St. Peter's Church in southern Texas, ending a dispute over religious rights that reached the Supreme Court, officials said Wednesday.

In a compromise agreement signed late Tuesday, the Roman Catholic parish in Boerne, a small south Texas city, will be allowed to tear down a section of the rear of the 74-year old church to attach a new sanctuary.
The city in turn agreed to donate a parcel of land to the church for utilities and parking space.

"You would see the new structure toward the rear," Boerne Mayor Patrick Heath said, "but the new structure would not overpower or compromise the continuing use of and architectural integrity of the historic structure."
The dispute in June reached the Supreme Court, which overturned the Religious Freedom Restoration Act of 1993 and sent the case back to a lower court for trial.

Attorneys representing the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of San Antonio claimed the city's denial of a demolition permit amounted to an illegal seizure of church property and interfered with its religious practices.
The city, struggling to hold onto its heritage in the face of rapid growth, said historic preservation ordinances allowed it to protect the stone church, which was built in 1923.
A final agreement is expected before the two sides are scheduled to appear at a hearing in federal court in San Antonio on Sept. 16.
